scope: All four files changed by the immutable lifecycle correction; prior multi-API admission, claim, result, observer and cleanup assertions carried forward by source review. Supporting installed transport implementations inspected where their semantics determine ownership.

findingResolution.reason: The unbounded in-process Nest setup and parent port reservation have been removed. Existing owned API children now provide real deadline-aware fixture HTTP. One shared action scope rejects pending operations, forbids new factories after cutoff, force-closes observer transports registered before connect, consumes late results/rejections and the Vitest cancellation signal. Cleanup has separately owned transports, explicit drain and bounded abortable reporting.

checks.result: DeadlineScope checks its absolute deadline before enqueuing an operation and again before invoking the factory. Expiry synchronously invokes registered force-closers and rejects outstanding waiters. Promise handlers consume late resolution/rejection, remove pending entries and reject completion after the deadline.

The same two Back/dist/main.js children bind HOST127.0.0.1 and PORT0. Their listener inode must belong to the owned child PID; the observed IPv4 loopback socket supplies the client URL. Distinct positive ports and four unique API/worker PIDs are required. The installed Joi port rule permits0. No parent Nest context, listener reservation or extra setup API remains.

A raw TCP Socket and close-event promise exist and are registered with the scope before Client.connect. The client has two-second connect/query/statement limits; cutoff destroys the supplied transport with an error. Installed pg source and the real stalled-startup socket test confirm this settles startup rather than suppressing its callback through Client.end. This transport also underlies a possible TLS wrapper.

The lazy client is registered before connect, has offline queuing disabled, two-second command/connect limits, retryStrategy returningnull and manual disconnect(false). Installed ioredis source confirms manual close cancels reconnect timers and prevents reconnect; the stalled socket test observes statusend and exactly one connection.

Every SQL call is executed through the scoped pg wrapper; getJob/getState and all other queue work are scoped factories. Read-only procfs operations, source/event-file reads, HTTP fetch/body reads and sleeps are bounded. The sequential SQL-to-getJob-to-getState overshoot path is removed. The synchronous provenance subprocesses use remaining-time timeouts.

Action observers are closed on enteringfinally. Existing owned-process stops remain two sequential phases with parallel workers and parallel APIs, each at most15s. Fresh cleanup observers use a5s scope and are closed before a1s drain checks pending operations, raw socket close, Redis end and retained queue-close promises. The3s reporting scope passes its signal towriteFile; expiry fails the test. A partial/unwritable report does not turn a failed pipeline into success.

45s actions +15s worker stop +15s API stop +5s cleanup +1s drain +3s reporting =84s allocated under the unchanged90s test timeout, leaving6s scheduling/report bookkeeping margin. No existing gate or timeout was extended.
